subject: Business Models
title: Amazon: Everything Store
description: A 60-second lesson on Amazon: Everything Store.

hook.text: Jeff Bezos started Amazon in his garage in 1994, selling books online. Just books.

buildup.text: He expanded to 'everything' and reinvested all profits into growth. Amazon lost money for years.

discovery.text: Amazon Web Services—cloud computing—now generates more profit than all the retail combined.

twist.text: Amazon's real product isn't goods. It's the infrastructure that moves and hosts everything.

climax.text: From a bookshop to a $1.5 trillion company powering half the internet. Commerce evolved.

punchline.text: Started with books. Now it runs half the internet.

quiz.question: What generates more profit for Amazon than retail?

details.summary: Amazon evolved from an online bookstore in 1994 to the everything store that dominates e-commerce, cloud computing, and digital entertainment..
details.whyItMatters: Amazon redefined customer expectations for price, selection, and delivery speed. Its marketplace, fulfillment network.
takeaways: Amazon started with books because they were ideal for online catalog sales
The flywheel strategy sacrificed profits to build scale that competitors cannot match
AWS cloud revenue subsidizes razor-thin retail margins and enables aggressive pricing

faq.question: What is the Amazon flywheel and how does it work?
faq.answer: Lower prices attract more customers. More customers attract more third-party sellers. More sellers increase selection. Better selection and more volume lower costs through supplier leverage and fulfillment efficiency. Lower costs enable lower prices..

faq.question: How did AWS become more profitable than Amazon's retail business?
faq.answer: Amazon built massive computing infrastructure for its own retail peak demand like Prime Day. Renting excess capacity became AWS. Cloud computing has 25 to 30 percent margins versus 2 to 5 percent in retail..
